sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Sharing the road with motorcycles, trucks, slow vehicles, animals and wildlife

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle looks farther away and faster than it is, so the safe assumption at an intersection is that it is closer and no faster than it appears [A01].
Why it matters: group motorcycle perception; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F06; confusables sec08-F06, sec08-F07
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A02
Passing a motorcycle means changing lanes completely because it owns a full lane, whereas passing a truck means waiting until its whole cab shows in your inside mirror before returning [A02].
Why it matters: group passing rules; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F12; confusables sec08-F12, sec08-F18
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A03
A truck's rear no-zone hides you from the driver and hides traffic from you, while its side no-zones are where a sudden truck lane change can hit you; the mirror test applies to both [A03].
Why it matters: group truck blind spots; difficulty medium; prereq sec08-F17; confusables sec08-F20, sec08-F21
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A03
The orange and red triangle on a farm vehicle marks a slow moving vehicle, a different meaning from the orange diamond that marks a work zone [A03].
Why it matters: group emblems; difficulty low; prereq sec08-F23; confusables sec08-F23, sec08-F24
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A04
Around animals the rule is silence and distance, no horn and no revving with four seconds behind, whereas around an aggressive driver the rule is calm avoidance without retaliation [A04].
Why it matters: group special road users; difficulty low; prereq sec08-F28; confusables sec08-F30, sec08-F28
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A04
Deer eyes shine in headlights but a moose's usually do not because of its height and dark color, which is why moose are the harder animal to spot at dusk [A04].
Why it matters: group wildlife; difficulty low; prereq sec08-F32; confusables sec08-F35, sec08-F33
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0046]
